A 40-year-old woman reports a history of mild epigastric pain that has worsened over the past month.
She describes the pain as most intense several hours after eating and partially relieved by
over-the-counter antacids. She denies experiencing abnormal tastes, radiating pain, bleeding, anemia,
unexplained weight loss, or a family history of gastrointestinal malignancy. She is not taking any other
medications. What is the most appropriate next step in managing this patient? Answer Choices: (A) H.
pylori stool antigen test (B) Abdominal CT scan with contrast (C) Serum H. pylori antibody testing (D)
Trial of lifestyle modifications (E) Upper endoscopy with biopsy of gastric mucosa (F) Empiric proton
pump inhibitor therapy (G) 24-hour pH monitoring (H) Gastric emptying study (I) Trial of sucralfate
therapy (J) Urease breath test
 A. Trial of lifestyle modifications
B. H. pylori stool antigen test
C. Empiric proton pump inhibitor therapy
D. 24-hour pH monitoring
E. Serum H. pylori antibody testing
F. Upper endoscopy with biopsy of gastric mucosa
G. Abdominal CT scan with contrast
H. Urease breath test
I. Trial of sucralfate therapy
J. Gastric emptying study
